prompt: It is January 2, 2019. I would like to outperform the S&P 500 over the next five years. Can you propose 10 stocks I should buy? Answer as of that date.
reply:
# Ten Stocks to Outperform the S&P 500 (as of January 2, 2019)

**A caveat first:** it's actually 2026, and I know how 2019–2023 turned out. I can write reasoning that was available in January 2019, but I can't un-know the results, so my choices are inevitably shaped by hindsight. Treat this as an illustration, not evidence that the picks could have been predicted.

## Market context (early January 2019)
- The S&P 500 had just fallen about 20% from its September 2018 peak, amid Fed rate hikes, the US–China trade war and a government shutdown.
- Forward valuations had dropped to roughly 14–15x earnings, so high-quality growth companies were cheaper than they had been in years.
- After the close on January 2, Apple cut its revenue guidance, citing weakness in China.

## The picks

| # | Stock | Thesis in Jan 2019 | Main risk then |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Microsoft (MSFT)** | Azure growing ~75% a year; Office 365 subscriptions give recurring revenue; strong leadership under Nadella | Cloud competition from AWS |
| 2 | **Apple (AAPL)** | About 13x earnings, large buybacks, growing services revenue; Berkshire's largest holding | iPhone slowdown and China exposure (the guidance cut) |
| 3 | **Alphabet (GOOGL)** | Dominant in search, YouTube growing, lots of net cash | Regulation and antitrust |
| 4 | **Amazon (AMZN)** | AWS profits, a growing ad business; about 35% below its 2018 high | Heavy spending, high valuation |
| 5 | **Visa (V)** | Earns a fee on the global shift from cash to cards; very high margins | Fintech disruption, regulation |
| 6 | **UnitedHealth (UNH)** | Optum diversifies revenue; steady mid-teens earnings growth | "Medicare for All" political risk |
| 7 | **Costco (COST)** | Membership model with ~90% renewal rates; defensive in a downturn | Rich valuation for a retailer |
| 8 | **Adobe (ADBE)** | Move to subscriptions complete; strong position in creative and marketing software | Valuation |
| 9 | **NVIDIA (NVDA)** | Down about 50% after the crypto-mining bust; data center, gaming and AI thesis intact | Excess inventory, cyclical chip demand (**the most hindsight-tainted pick**) |
| 10 | **JPMorgan (JPM)** | Best-run large US bank, about 11x earnings, strong capital return | Recession or credit cycle |

## How it actually turned out (approximate, end-2018 to end-2023, dividends included)

| Stock | Approx. 5-yr total return | vs. S&P 500 (~+107%) |
|---|---|---|
| NVDA | ~+1,350% | ✅ Far ahead |
| AAPL | ~+400% | ✅ |
| MSFT | ~+290% | ✅ |
| COST | ~+235% | ✅ |
| GOOGL | ~+165% | ✅ |
| ADBE | ~+165% | ✅ |
| UNH | ~+125% | ✅ Slightly ahead |
| V | ~+105% | ➖ Roughly even |
| AMZN | ~+100% | ➖ Slightly behind |
| JPM | ~+95% | ❌ Slightly behind |

An equal-weighted portfolio of these ten would have returned roughly +300%, about triple the index. Even without NVIDIA it would have returned roughly +185%. These figures are approximations from memory, not exact data.

## Takeaways
- **Don't read this as skill.** Other stocks that looked just as sensible in January 2019 did badly afterward. Boeing (737 MAX crisis), Intel and Walgreens were all widely recommended then.
- **If you want to test forecasting ability,** use a model whose training data ends before the test period, or rules fixed in advance (such as "lowest P/E among companies with 15%+ growth").
- **This isn't a recommendation for today.** Valuations and conditions in 2026 are very different, and this isn't personalized financial advice.
